findings.title: rollback_import_batch SECURITY DEFINER has no auth check — any authenticated user can mass-delete accounts/policies across all tenants
findings.description: The function `rollback_import_batch(UUID)` is SECURITY DEFINER (bypasses RLS) and is granted EXECUTE to `authenticated`. It contains zero authorization checks — no is_staff(), no is_agency_member(), no workspace validation. It soft-deletes all accounts, contacts, and policies matching a batch_id across the entire database regardless of workspace boundaries.
findings.impact: Any authenticated user (including customer portal users with account_memberships) can soft-delete entire import batches belonging to any workspace. This is a destructive cross-tenant data loss vulnerability. An attacker who enumerates or guesses batch UUIDs can systematically wipe agency data.
attack_path: 1. Attacker authenticates as any user (including a customer portal user via account_memberships)
2. Attacker enumerates import_batches.id values (import_batches RLS uses is_staff() but the RPC bypasses RLS as SECURITY DEFINER)
3. Attacker calls: SELECT rollback_import_batch('target-batch-uuid')
4. All accounts, contacts, and policies in that batch are soft-deleted across all tenants
5. import_batches.status is set to 'rolled_back' confirming success
findings.remediation: Add `IF NOT public.is_staff() THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'permission denied'; END IF;` at the top of the function body. Additionally verify workspace ownership of the batch: check that the batch belongs to a workspace the caller is a member of via agency_workspace_memberships.

findings.title: enqueue_outbox_event SECURITY DEFINER has no auth check — any authenticated user can inject automation events into any workspace
findings.description: The function `enqueue_outbox_event(UUID, TEXT, TEXT, UUID, JSONB, TEXT)` is SECURITY DEFINER and granted EXECUTE to `authenticated`. It accepts an arbitrary `p_workspace_id` parameter and inserts automation events into `automation_event_outbox` for that workspace with no verification that the caller is a member of that workspace or is staff.
findings.impact: Any authenticated user can inject forged automation events into any workspace's outbox. Depending on how downstream automation consumers process these events, this could trigger unauthorized actions (email sends, workflow executions, data modifications) in victim workspaces.
attack_path: 1. Attacker authenticates as any user
2. Attacker calls: SELECT enqueue_outbox_event('victim-workspace-id', 'policy_created', 'policy', 'any-uuid', '{"malicious": true}')
3. Event is inserted into automation_event_outbox for the victim workspace
4. Downstream automation consumers process the event, potentially triggering emails, workflows, or data mutations in the victim's context
findings.remediation: Add an auth guard: `IF NOT public.is_agency_member(p_workspace_id) THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'permission denied'; END IF;` at the top of the function. Alternatively restrict EXECUTE to service_role only if the function is only intended for server-side use.

findings.title: cancel_outbox_events SECURITY DEFINER has no auth check — any authenticated user can cancel all pending automation events across all workspaces
findings.description: The function `cancel_outbox_events(UUID, TEXT, TEXT)` is SECURITY DEFINER, granted EXECUTE to `authenticated`, and has no auth check. When called with `p_workspace_id = NULL` (the default), it cancels ALL pending/failed events across ALL workspaces in `automation_event_outbox`. Even with a workspace_id provided, there is no verification the caller belongs to that workspace.
findings.impact: Any authenticated user can disable all pending automations across the entire platform (denial of service for all tenants), or selectively sabotage a specific workspace's automations. This is both a cross-tenant integrity violation and a platform-wide availability attack.
attack_path: 1. Attacker authenticates as any user
2. Attacker calls: SELECT cancel_outbox_events(NULL, NULL, 'pwned')
3. ALL pending and failed automation events across ALL workspaces are set to 'cancelled'
4. Downstream automation processing stops for all tenants
findings.remediation: Add auth guard: require is_staff() AND if p_workspace_id is provided, require is_agency_member(p_workspace_id). If p_workspace_id is NULL (cancel-all), require a higher privilege (admin role check or restrict to service_role only).

findings.title: account_relationship_suggestions table has no RLS — any authenticated user can read/write all relationship suggestions cross-tenant
findings.description: The table `account_relationship_suggestions` is created without `ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`. In Supabase, the `authenticated` role has default DML privileges on public schema tables. Without RLS, any authenticated user can SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE all rows in this table regardless of workspace boundaries. The table contains from_account/to_account UUIDs, relationship types, signals (shared_phone, shared_address), and reasoning — which reveals customer relationships and PII-adjacent signals.
findings.impact: Any authenticated user (including portal customers) can: (1) enumerate all pending relationship suggestions to discover customer connections across tenants, (2) insert fake suggestions to mislead staff into creating incorrect relationships, (3) dismiss legitimate suggestions to prevent proper dedup, (4) confirm suggestions to create unauthorized relationship edges.
attack_path: 1. Attacker authenticates as any user (even a portal customer)
2. Attacker queries: SELECT * FROM account_relationship_suggestions
3. All cross-tenant suggestions are returned, revealing account IDs, relationship signals, and reasoning
4. Attacker can also: UPDATE account_relationship_suggestions SET status = 'dismissed' to suppress legitimate dedup
findings.remediation: Add: `ALTER TABLE public.account_relationship_suggestions ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;` and create a policy restricting access to staff within the workspace of the referenced accounts: `CREATE POLICY ars_staff ON public.account_relationship_suggestions FOR ALL USING (public.is_staff()) WITH CHECK (public.is_staff());`

findings.title: account_aliases table has no RLS — any authenticated user can read/write all account aliases cross-tenant
findings.description: The table `account_aliases` is created without `ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`. No RLS is ever enabled on this table in any subsequent migration. The table stores nicknames, maiden names, DBAs, former names, and misspellings for accounts — all of which are identity data that should be tenant-scoped. In Supabase default configuration, `authenticated` has full DML access to public schema tables without RLS.
findings.impact: Any authenticated user can read all aliases across all tenants (information disclosure of identity data), insert fake aliases to poison search results and enable social engineering, or delete aliases to disrupt identity resolution.
attack_path: 1. Attacker authenticates as any user
2. Attacker queries: SELECT aa.*, a.name, a.email FROM account_aliases aa JOIN accounts a ON a.id = aa.account_id
3. All aliases across all tenants are returned (bypasses accounts RLS because the join fetches alias data first)
4. Attacker can INSERT aliases for accounts in other workspaces to manipulate search/identity resolution
findings.remediation: Add: `ALTER TABLE public.account_aliases ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;` and create a workspace-scoped policy: `CREATE POLICY aliases_staff ON public.account_aliases FOR ALL USING (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM accounts a JOIN agency_workspace_memberships m ON m.agency_workspace_id = a.agency_workspace_id WHERE a.id = account_aliases.account_id AND m.user_id = auth.uid() AND m.status = 'active')) WITH CHECK (...same...);`

findings.title: account_relationships RLS checks 'any active membership' not 'same workspace' — allows cross-tenant relationship data access
findings.description: The RLS policies on `account_relationships` (SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE) only check `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM agency_workspace_memberships m WHERE m.user_id = auth.uid() AND m.status = 'active')` — meaning any user who is a staff member of ANY workspace can read and mutate ALL relationship edges across ALL workspaces. The policy does not verify that the accounts in the relationship belong to the caller's workspace.
findings.impact: In a multi-tenant deployment, staff in Workspace A can read all account relationships in Workspace B, revealing the ownership structure, family connections, and business affiliations of another agency's entire book. They can also insert/delete edges to corrupt another agency's relationship graph.
attack_path: 1. Staff user authenticates (member of Workspace A)
2. Staff queries: SELECT * FROM account_relationships (no workspace filter in RLS)
3. ALL relationship edges across ALL workspaces are returned
4. Staff can also INSERT edges linking accounts in Workspace B, corrupting their graph
5. The SECURITY DEFINER functions get_account_relationships() and get_account_cluster() compound this by bypassing even this weak RLS
findings.remediation: Change the RLS policies to verify workspace membership for the specific accounts: `USING (EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM accounts a JOIN agency_workspace_memberships m ON m.agency_workspace_id = a.agency_workspace_id WHERE a.id IN (account_relationships.from_account, account_relationships.to_account) AND m.user_id = auth.uid() AND m.status = 'active'))`. This ensures edges are only visible to members of the accounts' workspace.

findings.title: get_account_cluster SECURITY DEFINER has no workspace check — any staff user can traverse any account's full relationship cluster cross-tenant
findings.description: The function `get_account_cluster(uuid)` is SECURITY DEFINER, granted to `authenticated`, and only checks `is_staff()` without verifying the caller has workspace access to the target account. It performs a recursive 5-hop traversal returning account names, types, policy counts, premium amounts, and expiration dates — all bypassing RLS.
findings.impact: Any staff user in any workspace can call this function with an account_id from another workspace and receive the full cluster: every related account, their business/household structure, policy counts, premium totals, and next expiration dates. This is a complete cross-tenant book-of-business disclosure.
attack_path: 1. Staff user in Workspace A authenticates
2. Staff calls: SELECT * FROM get_account_cluster('account-id-in-workspace-b')
3. Function returns up to 5 hops of relationship graph with enriched data (names, premiums, policy counts)
4. Staff learns the full organizational structure and premium values of Workspace B's customers
findings.remediation: After the is_staff() check, verify workspace membership: look up the target account's agency_workspace_id and call is_agency_member(). Additionally, the recursive traversal should be bounded to accounts within the same workspace to prevent cross-tenant cluster walks.

findings.title: get_account_relationships SECURITY DEFINER has no workspace or staff check — leaks cross-tenant relationship data
findings.description: The function `get_account_relationships(uuid)` is SECURITY DEFINER with `SET search_path` but contains NO auth checks in its body. It directly queries account_relationships (bypassing RLS due to DEFINER) and joins accounts to return names, types, premium summaries for any account_id passed. Granted to `authenticated`.
findings.impact: Any authenticated user (including portal customers) can call this function with any account_id and receive all relationship edges and connected account details (names, goes_by, type, policy count, premium) — a cross-tenant information disclosure.
attack_path: 1. Any authenticated user (including portal customer) calls: SELECT * FROM get_account_relationships('any-account-uuid')
2. Function executes as postgres owner, bypassing RLS on both account_relationships and accounts
3. Returns all relationship edges with enriched data for the target account
findings.remediation: Add `IF NOT public.is_staff() THEN RETURN; END IF;` (convert to plpgsql) and add workspace verification: verify the target account's workspace matches the caller's active membership via is_agency_member().

findings.title: renewal_mark_renewed/renewal_mark_lost/renewal_reopen check is_staff() but not workspace — cross-tenant policy/renewal mutation
findings.description: The renewal terminal RPCs (renewal_mark_renewed, renewal_mark_lost, renewal_reopen) are SECURITY DEFINER functions that check is_staff() but never verify the caller has workspace access to the specific renewal/policy/account being modified. Any staff user from any workspace can mark renewals as renewed/lost/reopened and mutate policies in other workspaces.
findings.impact: Staff from Workspace A can close, reopen, or modify renewals and policies belonging to Workspace B. renewal_mark_renewed writes new policy terms (premium, dates, policy_number). renewal_mark_moved creates new policies. renewal_reopen reactivates cancelled policies. All are cross-tenant mutations.
attack_path: 1. Staff in Workspace A authenticates
2. Staff calls: SELECT renewal_mark_renewed('renewal-in-workspace-b', 'policy-in-workspace-b', 'account-in-workspace-b', 'POL-123', 50000, 'annual', '2027-01-01', '2028-01-01', null)
3. Workspace B's renewal is marked renewed, policy terms are overwritten with attacker-supplied values
4. A note is inserted on Workspace B's account
findings.remediation: After is_staff() check, look up the account's agency_workspace_id (join through renewal -> policy -> account or renewal -> account) and verify is_agency_member(workspace_id). Apply the same pattern used in void_certificate: `IF NOT (public.is_staff() AND public.is_agency_member(v_workspace)) THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'staff only'; END IF;`
